newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile says copper price reflects market situation.
newsitem.headline: Chile says copper price reflects market situation.

text.p: Recent rises in international copper prices reflect falls in inventories and are a natural reaction to supply and demand in the world market, said acting Mining Minister Sergio Hernandez.
"The copper market is reacting in a healthy way to the relation of supply and demand," Hernandez told a news conference. "Prices are clearly reacting to very low inventories."
Current copper prices are likely to be maintained toward the end of the year, provided basic market conditions do not change, he said.
Copper prices rose to close to $1.04/pound on the London Metal Exchange Monday from Friday's close of $1.01.
Chile is the world's largest copper producer with output of nearly 2.5 million tonnes last year.
